messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High OOM rate detected on decode-service-prod (node-group-decoder-2). 18 CUDA OOMs in the last 5m, ~22% request drops on streaming route. Pager triggered.

nisha: seeing the same in monitoring — CUDA "cuMemAlloc" failures + container restarts. Spike started ~1749999978.

samir: I'm on-call for infra, jumping in. any customer-facing errors reported?

cs-lead: CS reports a customer experiencing ~5% request failures on long generations. Not widespread yet but visible.

ops-oncall: taking immediate containment: cordoning node-group-decoder-2 and draining active pods. running drain now.

```
kubectl cordon node-group-decoder-2
kubectl drain node-group-decoder-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

marta: logs from one of the restarted containers show repeated allocation failures inside the decoder loop, stack:
```
E 2026-03-14T14:33:02Z decoder.cpp:312 alloc failed: cuMemAlloc 0x0 -> out of memory
W 2026-03-14T14:33:02Z runtime.cpp:88 falling back to spill-to-disk (slow)
```

nisha: quick triage — I see an inbound traffic pattern with very large generation lengths. Many requests didn't set `max_tokens` and the route default allows up to 8192. Looks like a misconfigured client or a prompt that triggers runaway generation.

samir: ok. apply a quick server-side ceiling for the streaming route to stop long tails. will push an emergency route override to 512 tokens.

samir: command: `POST /internal/route-overrides {"route":"/v1/stream-gen","max_tokens":512}`

ops-oncall: override applied. routing logs: `route_override_applied route=/v1/stream-gen max_tokens=512 by=samir`. Confirming reduced tail latency.

incident-bot: Note: fallback activation: system started routing overflow to a smaller quantized variant `redwood-7b-q4` for >1s stalls to reduce memory pressure.

marta: we still observed 2 node restarts due to `cuCtxDestroy` timeout and subsequent kernel-level errors — looks like GPU memory fragmentation aggravated by long decode loops.

nisha: mitigation checklist we just executed: 1) global route override to 512 tokens 2) cordon/drain of problematic node group 3) fallback to smaller model variant 4) hotpatch to freeze canary deploys for decode-service.

cs-lead: sent initial customer notification: "We detected elevated errors for long streaming requests and applied temporary safeguards (token cap + fallback). We're monitoring and will follow up with details." :white_check_mark:

eng-oncall: I will take a full timeline and postmortem. next steps: capture heap profiles from crashed pods, collect kernel logs from nodes, and replay offending request patterns in staging.

samir: immediate follow-ups (action items):
- add server-side hard cap at 1024 tokens when clients omit max_tokens (spring config toggle)
- create alert for route-level max_tokens drift and for sudden increase in average generation length
- add an e2e test simulating runaway generation to prevent regressions

ops-oncall: nodes are stable. no CUDA OOMs in the last 10m, drop rate down to <1%. Keeping pager open for 2h for watch.

marta: captured a representative request payload and stored in incident artifacts: `/artifacts/1749999991/runaway-sample.json` — includes prompt, headers, and stack traces.

nisha: adding incident tag `decode-runaway-max-tokens` and assigning to eng-ml (safety) and eng-runtime (allocator/GC).

cs-lead: follow-up message to customer scheduled for EOD with timeline and mitigation details.

samir: closing notes: this was a configuration + safety gap (no server-side ceiling + permissive route default). temporary controls fixed immediate impact. longer-term: make hard caps opt-out instead of opt-in, improve model fallback heuristics, and tune GC/allocator to handle fragmentation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager status: open (watching period)."
